svg.title: OKLab and OKLCH: three color-ramp comparisons
svg.desc: Three scenarios, each showing eleven steps in OKLab and OKLCH. A marks an exact input anchor. A star marks a generated sample mapped into sRGB for display. One blue seed gives identical displayed rows under these endpoint choices; related hues differ modestly; contrasting hues give a muted OKLab midpoint and a pink OKLCH midpoint.
svg.text: Same anchors, same light/dark targets, different interpolation paths.
A Exact seed anchor * Mapped into sRGB for display · 11 steps, opaque colors, Culori 4.0.2
Identical displayed HEX values for this recipe: the seed and both outer targets share one hue.
Three light-end samples in each row were gamut-mapped. This is not a general claim that both spaces always match.
The middle stays blue in both. At 500: OKLab #4986f0; OKLCH #2889f6, with slightly higher chroma.
The differences are between the anchors; the same-hue outer segments match. No samples were gamut-mapped.
At 500: OKLab #938ea4 is muted; OKLCH #df57a9 follows the shorter hue arc through pink and purple.
This is a visibly different palette, not simply a more accurate blend. No samples were gamut-mapped.
Linear segments use numeric step positions. Light target: L .97 / C .015; dark target: L .20 / C .03.
Each outer target uses its nearest seed hue. OKLCH takes the shorter hue arc. HEX is the 8-bit sRGB display result.
Exploration · 21 November 2026 · Manual anchor placement; no Auto algorithm or production recipe selected.
